page: Amazon Web Services x8i.64xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance managed by the Nitro hypervisor. The underlying platform incorporates 128 physical Intel cores clocked at 3.9 GHz, with 2 threads per core delivering 256 dedicated vCPUs. The primary hardware asset is a 4096 GB RAM footprint, establishing an expansive memory-to-core allocation of 16 GB per vCPU. Hardware GPU acceleration is not present in this configuration.

Storage and networking profiles prioritize high-speed network transit over local persistence. The server includes no bundled local NVMe storage, meaning all persistence requirements rely on network-attached storage architectures. Networking performance provides an 80 Gbps baseline bandwidth capacity, enabling continuous high-throughput communication with external volumes and cluster nodes.

From an architectural perspective, cost efficiency is achieved by consolidating multi-terabyte working sets onto a single computing node, avoiding the network overhead and serialization latency of distributed computing topologies. Tradeoffs involve strict dependence on remote storage volumes for disk operations and managing high-density thread scheduling. The hardware profile fits enterprise in-memory databases, massive caching engines, large-scale batch processing, and memory-bound analytics pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services x8i.64xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by Intel x86_64 architecture. The system provides 128 physical cores and 256 dedicated vCPUs clocked at 3.9 GHz, coupled with 4096 GB of system RAM to establish a memory-dense ratio of 16 GB per vCPU. The server lacks local storage arrays and hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating network storage attachments for persistent state management. A baseline network bandwidth of 80 Gbps facilitates heavy remote data ingest and multi-node synchronization. Economically, the profile targets single-system consolidation of massive in-memory datasets, trading off local disk throughput for immense memory capacity and dedicated execution threads. The instance configuration is well aligned for large enterprise in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, large-scale data science pipelines, and data analytics architectures requiring multi-terabyte working sets.
